summary: I pass on all three markets. Milwaukee is the favorite at -130 and the case is real: Logan Henderson has an ERA of 2.4712 against 3.2108 for Michael King, and MIL has the better run differential per game, 1.319 against 0.259. But the books' own de-vigged number for MIL is 0.5535, and that already reflects most of the starter and team-quality gap, so I do not see what the price misses. King's FIP of 4.1311 and recent ERA of 5.2941 lean toward MIL, but Henderson has only 98.33 innings this year. Lineups are not posted, and there is no matchup history or standings snapshot, so any lean rests on thin ground. On the run line, SD +1.5 at -185 is too expensive to chase, and MIL -1.5 at +165 needs a bigger win than the evidence supports. The total of 7 is priced almost level, with the over at 0.5092 fair probability, a retractable roof and a wind of 11.9 mph that I cannot read without knowing the roof status. The market is probably right on all three.

case_against.claim: Henderson's 2.4712 ERA sits 1.0315 runs below his 3.5027 FIP, so his ERA likely flatters him over a 98.33 inning sample, and the starter Milwaukee's lineup faces has allowed 0.2852 wOBA to left-handed hitters against 0.3019 to right-handed, so Milwaukee's six left-handed bats do not get the usual platoon lift.

derived.note: Henderson's FIP minus his ERA: how far his ERA runs below his FIP.

reasons.claim: Milwaukee has the better starter on the season numbers: Henderson's ERA and FIP are both lower than King's, and his strikeout-minus-walk rate is far higher.
Milwaukee has been the stronger team by run differential, and is far better at home than San Diego is on the road.
San Diego's Adrian Morejon is likely unavailable after 31 pitches yesterday, and every Milwaukee reliever is listed as available, so the late innings tilt toward Milwaukee.
Milwaukee's posted lineup has hit well against the sinker, the primary pitch of the starter it faces, over a large sample.
The books already lean Milwaukee, and my number is only a few points above theirs, so this is a small disagreement with the price rather than a big one.

calls.what_would_change_it: A scratch of Henderson, a Milwaukee lineup change that removes key bats, or a price worse than -138 would turn this into a pass.

summary:
I lean Milwaukee at -128. Logan Henderson has the better numbers going in, with a 2.4712 ERA and 3.5027 FIP against 3.2108 and 4.1311 for Michael King, and Milwaukee's run differential per game is 1.319 against San Diego's 0.259. Adrian Morejon looks likely unavailable for San Diego after 31 pitches yesterday, while every Milwaukee reliever is listed as available. I put Milwaukee a few points above the books' 0.5511, so my number is only a little off the price. The case against is that Henderson's ERA runs well under his FIP.

I pass on the run line. The packet says nothing about margin beyond the moneyline view, and SD +1.5 at -185 is already expensive, so I think the market is about right. I also pass on the total of 7, which the books split almost evenly. Both starters are strong, the wind is 12.1 mph from 306 degrees, and the packet does not say if the roof is open. Standings and team totals are missing, and no props were analyzed.
